summary: Throughout the course of the hackathon, Team Deuterium has worked in a synchronous manner to create a website that monitors fluctuations on the Earth's surface using existing NASA Earth models in order to conceive accurate and reliable readings, Earthify. Earthify utilizes a wide array of different variables that make it adept at fulfilling the challenge provided. The challenge asks for a project that monitors changes in the Earth's surface and classifies them as significant or minor. This is precisely what Team Deuterium has achieved in its Earth data tracking website. Earthify can be a vital tool for aspiring meteorologists, agriculturists, climate enthusiasts, and many more due to its ability to display complicated data in a digestible and understandable manner. Team Deuterium firmly believes that Earthify will have a profound impact on the field of climate science as a whole due to its versatility and ease of use.
details:
Earthify is a dynamic, interactive website that tracks the fluctuations of certain variables, such as air pressure, solar radiation, wind speed, and relative humidity, drawing its information straight from existing NASA Earth models. The process of using the website starts when the user inputs a specific location, filter, and date into the respective boxes. This allows the website to fetch information from NASA's official APIs, making it accurate and reliable. The user can then see an overlay of the filtered data over a map of the Earth.

The impact of this project is mainly directed towards agriculturists, meteorologists, and climate enthusiasts who need a quick visual demonstration of the changes in the Earth's atmosphere. Earthify’s main source code was written through the use of JavaScript React in VS Code. Artificial Intelligence was used as a development aid in order to act as a catalyst for our existing ideas, knowledge, and skills to speed up the process, alongside diminishing the margin of repetition. All implementation and a vast majority of the development were done purely by the programmer of Team Deuterium.

Our project is highly innovative, as it allows the user to filter out the variable that they want and displays a very appealing cover page. We considered ease of use, understandability, and pragmatic implementation when building the framework of our project. In terms of factors in the Earth's atmosphere, we used air pressure, solar radiation, wind speed, and relative humidity in order to provide users with a wide range of variables.
